title: A decision-focused 60-minute readout
objective: Cut a 40-slide product introduction down to an executive opening.
clearance: Rewritten draft; pending SME and partner clearance

blocks.x: Executives give you an hour. Spend most of it on their workflows, their value, and the decision, not on a product tour.
Glean's checklist frames the readout as a sequence: use case readout → future state → value → decision and next steps. A concise executive narrative covers:

items: The objective and context, including why this decision now.
The prioritized workflows, with before and after.
The business value and its assumptions.
Success criteria and the recommended validation path.

blocks.x: These timings are this course's design and fit a 60-minute session. They are not a mandated agenda.
Glean's playbook says repositioning Glean matters, especially with a new executive sponsor, but should take no more than five minutes. Give a high-level overview, then move to the customer's work.
A readout is a decision meeting. Most of the time goes to the customer's evidence and the decision, not the product.

blocks.title: A decision-focused readout narrative
blocks.alt: A five-part readout narrative: restate the three whys, play back what was heard, show the value range and assumptions, show a short tailored demonstration, and ask for the decision and validation path.
